claude_proposed_widenings.name: cunning_strike_option
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Devious Strikes adds options to the Cunning Strike menu. Each option triggers on a Sneak Attack hit (not an independent activation), costs a subset of the rogue's sneak attack dice, and fires a save-gate rider on the target. No existing class-feature family models menu-option mechanics subordinate to an attack trigger with a dice-pool cost.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "The following effects are now among your Cunning Strike options." — the feature is a menu extension, not a standalone activated ability.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: sneak_attack_dice_cost resource
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Each option costs dice from the rogue's per-attack Sneak Attack pool (2d6, 3d6, or 6d6). This is not a use_count, not a spell_slot, and not a charge — it is a fractional expenditure from a per-attack dice pool. No existing UseCountResource or RestResetCadence models this.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "Daze (Cost: 2d6)", "Obscure (Cost: 3d6)", "Knock Out (Cost: 6d6)" — cost is in sneak attack dice, not feature uses.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: Condition enum: blinded, unconscious
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Condition surface type is closed to only 'prone'. Obscure requires 'blinded' and Knock Out requires 'unconscious'. Both are standard SRD 5.2.1 conditions used as apply_condition targets.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn" (Obscure); "it has the Unconscious condition for 1 minute" (Knock Out).

claude_proposed_widenings.name: repeat_save surface type
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Knock Out requires the target to repeat the CON save at the end of each of its turns. The v4 taxonomy includes 'repeat_save' as a resolution atom, but types.ts has no surface representation for repeat saves in class feature riders.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "The Unconscious target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success."

claude_proposed_widenings.name: restrict_turn_economy
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Daze restricts the target to choosing exactly one of {move, take an action, take a bonus action} on its next turn. This is distinct from the existing restrict_action_set atom (which filters which action type is valid within an extra-action grant on the user) — it is a constraint on the target's entire turn allocation. No existing effect atom covers this semantics.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: "on its next turn, it can do only one of the following: move or take an action or a Bonus Action" (Daze).
